newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to use high rates to curb speculators.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to use high rates to curb speculators.

text.p: Thailand's central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday that the bank would continue its policy of keeping domestic interest rates high as a measure to deter speculators in the baht.

He told reporters there were also no immediate plans to widen the central bank's current fixed four-satang trading range for the baht between commercial banks and the Bank of Thailand until the time was right.
He clarified that the right time for any change would be when Thailand's economic fundamentals improved and became more stable.

"We have to look at the economic picture first to see if there is a turnaround. For the moment, we will rely on high and stable interest rates and will continue to watch the foreign exchange markets situation for a while," he said.

When asked if the high rates policy would hurt some financially-strapped local firms, Rerngchai said that the central bank would help out any finance firms by providing sufficient funding to meet their short-term needs.
"We have channels to do that," he said.

The governor did not specify what were the high rates he had referred to but he said they should not be as high as they were last Friday. Dealers said the overnight interbank rate shot up to 25-28 percent last Friday on seasonal demand for funds during the Lunar New Year, demand from banks to meet BOT reserve requirements and heavy withdrawals by some state enterprises.
